title: Ryan Veterinary Hospital
organization: University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine
summary: A university teaching hospital for dogs and cats with emergency, intensive care, surgery, neurology, oncology, internal medicine, cardiology, rehabilitation-adjacent specialty care, and other referral services.
useWhen: Use this when a dog has a true emergency, needs hospital-level critical care, or has a complex specialty case that a primary veterinarian wants referred.
team: The hospital publishes Emergency & Critical Care leadership including Deborah C. Silverstein, DVM, DACVECC and ICU service head Lori S. Waddell, DVM, DACVECC.
details: Emergency service is published as open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
The hospital asks families to call first because capacity and triage can change.
Patients are seen by medical priority; wait times vary with caseload.

title: William R. Pritchard Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital
organization: UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine
coverage: Davis, California; appointments and referrals from beyond the region
summary: A public university veterinary medical center with emergency and critical care, advanced imaging, surgery, oncology, neurology, internal medicine, cardiology, hemodialysis and clinical-trial access.
useWhen: Use this when a senior dog needs immediate stabilization, a complex second opinion, or a university specialty service in Northern California.
team: UC Davis states that its emergency room is led by board-certified faculty specialists and supported by residents, interns and veterinary technicians.
details: Small-animal emergency care is published as available 24 hours a day, every day of the year.
The hospital asks owners to call ahead when possible but does not require an appointment for emergency-room arrival.
For hospitalized patients, the hospital says it provides a written estimate and discusses charges before care proceeds.

title: Veterinary Teaching Hospital
mode: 24/7 emergency; primary care within service area; referral specialties
summary: A teaching hospital providing emergency and critical care, specialty referral care, and small-animal community practice. Specialty appointments generally require referral from a primary veterinarian.
useWhen: Use this for an emergency in the region or when a primary veterinarian is arranging a referral for a complex medical, neurologic, surgical or rehabilitation-related need.
team: The emergency service is publicly described as led by a board-certified emergency and critical care specialist; Bobbi Conner, DVM, DACVECC is listed on the current care-team page.
details: The published emergency line is staffed 24/7/365.
The hospital describes a teaching model where students work under direct clinical supervision.
The client page explains that inpatient care requires a written estimate and a prepayment or deposit.

title: Cornell University Hospital for Animals: Companion Animal Hospital
organization: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
coverage: Ithaca, New York and Central New York
summary: A university companion-animal hospital for dogs, cats, exotics and other domestic animals, with emergency access and specialty services through Cornell Veterinary Medicine.
useWhen: Use this when a dog needs emergency evaluation in Central New York or a university specialty service after discussion with a primary veterinarian.
team: Cornell publishes service-specific specialist teams through the University Hospital for Animals.
details: Cornell states that emergency support is available 24/7/365.
The emergency page lists this number for dogs, cats, exotics and companion animals.
For a non-emergency specialty visit, confirm referral and record requirements with the relevant service.

title: Behavior Medicine Service
organization: Cornell University Hospital for Animals and Duffield Institute for Animal Behavior
summary: A specialty behavior service for anxiety, fears, phobias, aggression and age-related behavior changes in companion animals, including senior-dog changes that need medical context.
useWhen: Use this when nighttime anxiety, fear, aggression, confusion or other behavior change needs a specialist conversation after urgent medical causes have been considered.
team: Cornell states that the service sits within both its University Hospital for Animals and the Duffield Institute for Animal Behavior.
details: Cornell says a primary-veterinarian referral is not required for this service.
An online behavior history form is required before scheduling.
The clinic asks owners to arrange medical records, recent test results and vaccination records before the visit.

title: Cornell University Veterinary Specialists
organization: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
summary: Cornell lists this Stamford hospital as a dogs-and-cats location in its emergency contact directory.
useWhen: Use this to call and confirm current emergency or specialty availability in the Stamford area before travel.
details: Cornell publishes this location as a separate dogs-and-cats contact.
Call directly to confirm hours, service availability and referral requirements before leaving home.

title: UF Small Animal Hospital
organization: University of Florida College of Veterinary Medicine
coverage: Gainesville, Florida and Southeast referral region
summary: A university small-animal hospital offering 24-hour emergency and critical care, ICU support, advanced diagnostics and specialty services for dogs and other companion animals.
useWhen: Use this for a serious emergency in the Gainesville area or for a specialty referral involving oncology, internal medicine, dentistry, cardiology or complex surgery.
team: UF describes a board-certified emergency and critical care team providing round-the-clock evaluation and ICU care.
details: UF states that its emergency service is available 24/7, including holidays.
The hospital says emergencies can be walk-ins and referrals; some specialty services have referral requirements.
For emergency referrals, UF asks callers to confirm capacity and the fastest appropriate option.

title: Veterinary Medical Center: Small Animal Clinic
organization: Michigan State University College of Veterinary Medicine
coverage: East Lansing, Michigan and Michigan referral region
summary: A university medical center with small-animal emergency care, more than 20 specialty services, veterinary social work, and a teaching-hospital team model.
useWhen: Use this for a small-animal emergency in the region or when your veterinarian recommends collaborative specialty care in Michigan.
team: MSU states that specialty areas are staffed by licensed veterinarians, residents, interns, veterinary technicians and supervised students.
details: MSU publishes the small-animal emergency and appointment line as available 24 hours.
The hospital describes more than 20 companion-animal specialty services.
Veterinary Social Work is listed among its client-support services.

title: Small Animal Teaching Hospital
organization: Texas A&M Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital
coverage: College Station, Texas and Texas referral region
mode: Hospital appointments and emergency call line
summary: A veterinary teaching hospital for companion animals with emergency contact, specialty appointments and referral pathways through Texas A&M Veterinary Medicine.
useWhen: Use this for a small-animal emergency in College Station or when a veterinarian is arranging a complex specialty referral.
address: 408 Raymond Stotzer Parkway, College Station, TX 77845
details: Texas A&M publishes the small-animal hospital appointment and emergency contact line.
Its referral guidance says emergency callers should speak with a staff member rather than leave a message.
Confirm which specialty service requires referral and what records should travel with the dog.

title: Veterinary Emergency Group: Center City
summary: A Philadelphia emergency-hospital location listed by Penn Vet in its publicly published referral contacts.
useWhen: Use this only for urgent or emergency concerns. Call before travel to confirm current capacity, arrival instructions and any triage considerations.
details: Penn Vet's referral page lists this location as open 24/7.
The published referral page says to call first; emergency capacity can change rapidly.

title: Veterinary Emergency Group: Northern Liberties
summary: A 24-hour emergency hospital in Philadelphia's Northern Liberties neighborhood. Veterinary Emergency Group publishes walk-in emergency access and its current hospital contact details.
useWhen: Use this only for urgent or emergency concerns. Call before travel to confirm current capacity, arrival instructions and any triage considerations.
details: VEG publishes this hospital as open 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
Call before travel when possible so the team can give current arrival and triage guidance.

title: Deborah C. Silverstein, DVM, DACVECC
organization: Ryan Veterinary Hospital, University of Pennsylvania
mode: Published clinical-leadership profile; not a direct booking listing
summary: Penn Vet lists Dr. Silverstein as Chief of the Emergency & Critical Care section at Ryan Veterinary Hospital and as a professor in emergency and critical care.
useWhen: Use this profile to understand the published leadership behind a hospital service. For care, contact Ryan Veterinary Hospital rather than attempting to book an individual clinician here.
team: Published role: Chief, Section of Emergency & Critical Care, Ryan Veterinary Hospital.
details: Credential shown by Penn Vet: DACVECC, American College of Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care.
The ICU and emergency service are hospital team services, with triage and current capacity handled by the hospital.

title: Lori S. Waddell, DVM, DACVECC
organization: Ryan Veterinary Hospital, University of Pennsylvania
mode: Published clinical-leadership profile; not a direct booking listing
summary: Penn Vet lists Dr. Waddell as service head for the Intensive Care Unit at Ryan Veterinary Hospital and a professor of clinical critical care medicine.
useWhen: Use this as a transparent public profile of the ICU service leadership. For care and availability, contact the hospital's emergency or appointment line.
team: Published role: Service Head, Intensive Care Unit, Ryan Veterinary Hospital.
details: Credential shown by Penn Vet: DACVECC.
The hospital describes ICU care as a 24-hour team service involving faculty, residents, nurses and clinical staff.

title: Bobbi Conner, DVM, DACVECC
mode: Published clinician profile; not a direct booking listing
summary: Virginia Tech lists Dr. Conner as a Clinical Professor in Emergency and Critical Care Medicine on its small-animal emergency and critical-care team page.
useWhen: Use this profile to understand the credentialed leadership behind the Virginia Tech emergency service. For patient care, call the hospital's published line.
team: Published role: Clinical Professor, Emergency and Critical Care Medicine.
details: Credential shown by Virginia Tech: DACVECC.
The hospital's emergency page describes a team model with emergency clinicians and licensed veterinary technicians.

title: Dani McVety, DVM
mode: Public professional biography; not an individual booking listing
summary: Lap of Love's published media kit identifies Dr. McVety as founder and chief executive officer, with professional work in emergency medicine and end-of-life veterinary communication.
useWhen: Use this profile to understand a publicly named leader in veterinary end-of-life education. For local care, use the provider-network search and confirm the individual veterinarian assigned to your area.
team: Published role: Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Lap of Love.
details: The organization describes her as a veterinarian, speaker, author and educator on end-of-life veterinary topics.
This profile does not mean Dr. McVety is personally available for an appointment in a given location.

title: Mary Gardner, DVM
mode: Public professional biography; not an individual booking listing
summary: Lap of Love's published media material identifies Dr. Gardner as a cofounder of the organization and a veterinarian working in senior-pet and end-of-life education.
useWhen: Use this profile to understand the publicly named clinical leadership behind a national hospice network. For care, search the network by location and confirm the local veterinarian's availability.
team: Published role: Lap of Love cofounder.
details: The public media kit links her work to senior-pet and end-of-life education.
This is a background profile, not a representation that she is bookable in every location.

title: Kathleen Cooney, DVM, CHPV, CPEV, DACAW
mode: Public education profile; not a direct booking listing
summary: Merck Veterinary Manual identifies Dr. Cooney as Senior Director of Medical Education at the Companion Animal Euthanasia Training Academy and lists her end-of-life credentials.
useWhen: Use this profile to understand the published professional background behind euthanasia-care education. It is not a substitute for contacting a local licensed veterinarian about your dog.
team: Published role: Senior Director of Medical Education, Companion Animal Euthanasia Training Academy.
details: Published credentials include CHPV, CPEV and DACAW.
The profile is an educational credential source, not an appointment directory.

title: Alice Villalobos, DVM, DPNAP
coverage: Educational resource; not a current provider locator
summary: The Animal Welfare Institute credits Dr. Villalobos, a veterinary oncologist, with developing the HHHHHMM quality-of-life framework and the Pawspice hospice model for terminally ill pets.
useWhen: Use this to understand the origin of a widely referenced quality-of-life framework, then discuss the observations with your own veterinary team rather than relying on a score alone.
team: Publicly described role: veterinary oncologist and developer of the Pawspice quality-of-life framework.
details: The HHHHHMM framework considers hurt, hunger, hydration, hygiene, happiness, mobility and more good days than bad.
Use it to organize observations for a veterinary conversation; it is not a standalone decision tool.

title: Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation Service
coverage: Ithaca, New York; appointment-based specialty care
mode: Sports medicine, mobility evaluation and rehabilitation
summary: Cornell's specialty service evaluates lameness, osteoarthritis, mobility loss, recovery after surgery and performance injuries in companion animals.
useWhen: Use this when pain, weakness, slower rising, reduced endurance or recovery after surgery needs a structured mobility assessment and rehabilitation plan.
team: Cornell publishes a team of sports-medicine and rehabilitation faculty, residents, veterinarians and rehabilitation technicians.
details: The service lists gait analysis, diagnostic imaging, therapeutic exercise and rehabilitation planning among its capabilities.
Ask what records, imaging and referral information should be sent before the appointment.
Confirm the current appointment pathway and whether an initial examination is required before therapy begins.

title: Nutrition Service
coverage: Ithaca, New York; appointment-based specialty care
summary: Cornell's clinical nutrition service develops feeding plans for healthy pets and animals with medical conditions that affect appetite, weight or nutrient needs.
useWhen: Use this when weight loss, obesity, kidney or gastrointestinal disease, food intolerance, home-prepared diets or several diagnoses make feeding decisions difficult.
team: Cornell publishes this as a hospital specialty service supported by veterinary nutrition expertise.
details: Bring a complete diet history, including treats, supplements, table food and exact product names.
Ask whether recent bloodwork, weight history and body-condition scores should be sent in advance.
Do not discontinue a prescribed diet or add supplements before the veterinary team reviews the full medical picture.

title: Christopher Frye, DVM, DACVSMR
mode: Published specialist profile; appointments are made through the hospital service
summary: Cornell identifies Dr. Frye as Associate Professor and Section Chief of Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation.
useWhen: Use this profile to understand the board-certified leadership behind Cornell's mobility and rehabilitation service. Contact the hospital for current patient access.
team: Published role: Section Chief, Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation.
details: Cornell publishes the DACVSMR credential on the service's specialist page.
The service treats mobility and rehabilitation concerns as a team; this profile is not a promise that one clinician will personally manage every appointment.
